scope: How a delivery team maps and tracks the delivery dependencies it waits on (other teams, vendors, tasks, decisions; internal and external): each dependency's type, owner, status and need-by date, and how one at risk or blocked is flagged and escalated before it delays a milestone. General practice for any delivery team. Out of scope: software dependencies (libraries, OS frameworks), milestone dependency chains, cycle detection and the critical path (milestone-scheduling), and the general linking convention between records (project-record-linking).
research_type: How-to / troubleshooting (Product / how-to LOW-MEDIUM bar, broad independent consensus; no escalation). Metric claims take the Statistical MED-HIGH bar.

questions.text: Best practices: what is current best practice for this topic?
Known solutions: what solutions, patterns, libraries and tools already exist, and how do they compare?
Platform guidelines: what do the platform owners' own guidelines say, for each platform the topic touches (Apple, Android, Windows, web, the databases and runtimes concerned)?
The expert's view: if we hired an expert consultant in this topic, what would they tell us: what to do, what to avoid, and what people usually get wrong?

research_questions: Best practice: how should a delivery team map and track its dependencies on other teams, vendors, tasks and decisions: internal versus external, each with a type, an owner, a status and a need-by date?
Known solutions: how do dependency boards, SAFe's program board, RAID logs and the dependency links of Jira, Linear and GitHub Projects compare for tracking delivery dependencies?
Platform guidelines: what do the PMBOK Guide's schedule and stakeholder guidance, PRINCE2 and the scaled-agile frameworks (SAFe, LeSS) say about recording and managing dependencies between teams?
The expert's view: what do delivery leads say teams get wrong with dependencies (found late, no owner on the other side, status never updated), and what to do instead?

Blocked dependency flagging: find how teams mark a dependency at risk or blocked and escalate it before it delays a milestone, and state the status values a dependency carries and when a blocked one is escalated.

methodology.method: guidelines/researching/process/research-methodology-and-sources: orient and classify the domain (cross-team delivery dependencies; how-to), go to the method owners' own guides (Scrum Guide, Kanban Guide, SAFe, LeSS) and the trackers' own documentation (GitHub, Linear, Jira) first, then professional-body and institutional guidance (APM / INCOSE UK SIG, University of Essex Strategic Projects Office), then practitioner sources for what no primary covers; corroborate across independent publishers; record provenance at generation time.
methodology.search_strategy: WebSearch for each method owner's and tracker's own pages on dependencies, blocked work, impediments, flags and status updates; for PMI, PRINCE2 and ISO 21502 public material; and for practitioner work on blockers and dependency impact (Leopold and Magennis, Team Topologies, DORA). Every cited page fetched with WebFetch or downloaded with curl and read as text (APM PDF converted with pdftotext).
methodology.inclusion: Primary: method owners' guides (scrumguides.org, kanbanguides.org, framework.scaledagile.com, less.works), trackers' own documentation (docs.github.com, linear.app/docs, support.atlassian.com). Institutional / professional-body: APM / INCOSE UK Systems Thinking SIG guidance; University of Essex project-delivery guidance. Secondary, flagged in the trust basis: Atlassian's own articles on RAID logs and dependencies, prince2.wiki, InfoQ (Leopold and Magennis), Team Topologies, DORA, a wiki summary of a Magennis talk.
methodology.exclusion: Search-result snippets; pages that could not be fetched (pmi.org learning library 403, projectmanagement.com 403, iso.org 403, GAO schedule guide 403, local.gov.uk 403, project-management-basics.com PRINCE2 mirrors 404, Linear's old issue-relations URL which now redirects); exam-prep flashcards and SEO templates; any claim without a fetched quote.
methodology.scoring: guidelines/researching/evidence/verification-and-trust-scoring: Authority 30 + Independent corroboration 25 + Accuracy/verifiability 20 + Currency 10 + Transparency 15, capped by the domain bar (Product / how-to LOW-MEDIUM; Statistical MED-HIGH for metric claims), applying cite-the-claim-not-the-document, independence-before-corroboration, domain-stratified-trust, suppress-unsupported-confidence and provenance-at-generation-time.

summary: The three Worker Focus rules hold at SHOULD strength: sources independently classify dependencies as internal or external (APM quoting PRINCE2 and MSP, University of Essex, Leopold and Magennis), track each one's status and keep reviewing it (Essex, Atlassian, APM, Kanban Guide, Linear), and flag blocked or at-risk ones visibly (GitHub's Blocked icon, Linear's orange and red flags, Jira's Impediment flag and red off-track dependencies). The two Verify rules are supported only at SHOULD, not as must-hold checks: sources recommend recording a dependency's type and status and linking blocked work to what it blocks, but none requires it of every dependency, so both are unsupported at the stated strength and recorded as prior claims. The research finds six practices no rule covers: an owner agreed on both sides, a need-by date in a 'we depend on X to deliver Y by date Z' statement, a small status vocabulary (on track / at risk / off track plus blocked), escalation through a named cross-team forum or by exception before a milestone slips, logging an at-risk dependency as a risk, and reducing dependencies before tracking them. Apple, Android and Windows have no bearing on this topic.
open_questions: Whether the two Verify clauses (every dependency has a type and status; blocked or at-risk dependencies are linked to affected milestones or todos) stay as must-hold checks as a house convention, or are restated at SHOULD, the strength the sources support.

Which status vocabulary the cookbook adopts for a dependency: the trackers' project-health set (On track, At risk, Off track) plus Blocked and Done, or another set; the sources offer several and none is a standard.

What 'type' means for a dependency in the cookbook: internal versus external (PRINCE2), internal / intra / external (MSP, Essex), inward versus outward (APM), the PMBOK's mandatory / discretionary, or what the dependency is on (team, vendor, task, decision); the sources use all of these.

When a blocked or at-risk dependency is escalated: at a fixed review cadence, as soon as its need-by date is forecast to be missed (PRINCE2's manage-by-exception), or at a named forum such as SAFe's ART Sync; the sources give no single trigger.
Whether a dependency at risk is also entered as a risk (Essex, APM), which would couple this topic to risk-tracking, or stays only in the dependency record.
limitations: PMI's PMBOK Guide could not be read: pmi.org and projectmanagement.com returned 403 to every fetch, and no PMI-published public excerpt was reachable, so no claim cites PMI and the PMBOK's mandatory / discretionary / internal / external taxonomy is not used as a finding.
ISO 21502 and ISO 31000 could not be read: iso.org returned 403 and no public excerpt was found; no claim cites them.

PRINCE2's own manual (AXELOS / PeopleCert) was not reachable; its dependency definitions are taken from the APM / INCOSE UK guidance that quotes them, and its manage-by-exception rule from prince2.wiki, both secondary.

SAFe's article bodies are partly behind a login; only the publicly served sentences were usable, and SAFe's ROAM risk method and the ART planning board's dependency notation could not be quoted from Scaled Agile's own pages.
LeSS's own coordination guide was fetched; LeSS says nothing specific about a dependency status or an escalation trigger.

No study with a disclosed sample was found for any metric claim (dependency counts versus on-time delivery, or review cadence); the only quantitative claim (each dependency halves the chance of on-time completion) is a teaching model reported second-hand and is scored on the Statistical bar accordingly.
The GAO Schedule Assessment Guide and the UK Government Functional Standard GovS 002 could not be fetched (403) or did not expose dependency clauses.

citations.title: Troy Magennis - Solving the Hairy Problem of Team Dependencies
citations.author: Hans Samios

claims.source_type: personal notes summarising a conference talk (secondary)
claims.query: Troy Magennis dependencies probability on-time delivery each dependency halves

trust.basis: Metric claim on the Statistical bar: no study, sample or measure, a 50/50-per-dependency teaching model reported second-hand in a personal wiki; capped low; usable only as the direction of the effect, never as a figure. Second check 2026-11-24: refuted (quote-found yes, supports-claim partly): The page (notes on a Troy Magennis talk) supports "halves the chances" and "remove dependency - half chances of being delayed". It never compares removing a dependency with tracking it, so "worth more than tracking it" is an added conclusion; lowered 25->5.
